title: Reciprocal, Quotient and Pythagorean Identities
short: Rewrite trig expressions in terms of sine and cosine.

blocks.html: An identity is an equation that is true for every value where both sides are defined, like $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$ from the Pythagorean identity. A short list of identities lets you rewrite complicated expressions as simple ones. You do not need to memorize them as separate facts: they all come from the definitions and that one circle equation.

head: Kind
Identities
rows: $\csc x = \dfrac{1}{\sin x}$, $\sec x = \dfrac{1}{\cos x}$, $\cot x = \dfrac{1}{\tan x}$
$\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$, $\cot x = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}$

blocks.html: The reciprocal and quotient identities are the definitions of the four other functions. Divide $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$ by $\cos^2 x$: $\frac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} + 1 = \frac{1}{\cos^2 x}$, which is $\tan^2 x + 1 = \sec^2 x$. Divide by $\sin^2 x$ instead to get $1 + \cot^2 x = \csc^2 x$.
To simplify, rewrite everything in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$, combine fractions, and watch for $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x$ (or $1 - \cos^2 x$, $1 - \sin^2 x$) to replace.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: The two squares trade places as $x$ changes, but their sum (green) never moves off $1$.

blocks.title: Quotient identity
steps: $\sin x \cdot \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \cos x$, since the factor $\sin x$ cancels.

blocks.title: Common denominator
steps: In sines and cosines: $\dfrac{1}{\cos x} - \dfrac{\sin^2 x}{\cos x}$.
Same denominator: $\dfrac{1 - \sin^2 x}{\cos x} = \dfrac{\cos^2 x}{\cos x}$.

blocks.html: Cancelling a term instead of a factor: $\dfrac{1 - \sin x}{\sin x}$ is not $1 - 1$. You can only cancel something that multiplies the whole top and the whole bottom. Here the correct split is $\dfrac{1}{\sin x} - 1 = \csc x - 1$. Check any simplification by plugging in an angle such as $\frac{\pi}{6}$.
